content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents to identify all available project documents, especially candidate_specs.md and any simulation, rate, efficiency, threshold-scan, latency, or allocated-rate documents."},{"id":"s2","description":"Read candidate_specs.md. Extract the three allowed candidate algorithms, assign them numeric candidate IDs 1-3 in the listed order, and note any documented implementation constraints relevant to Level-1 operation."},{"id":"s3","description":"Read the simulation/performance documents for the three candidates. For thresholds in the allowed 20-60 GeV range, extract or interpolate the signal efficiency as a function of threshold for each candidate, focusing on thresholds that can satisfy the allocated trigger rate."},{"id":"s4","description":"Read the rate/allocation and hardware-latency documents. For each candidate, determine the lowest threshold between 20 and 60 GeV that is at or below the allocated trigger rate, and extract the corresponding latency on the Level-1 FPGA hardware."},{"id":"s5","description":"Apply the hard requirements: signal efficiency >=80%, latency <=4.0 us, threshold between 20 and 60 GeV, and rate <= allocated rate. Among passing options, choose the candidate/threshold with the highest signal efficiency. Use record_results to store numeric values for the recommended candidate ID, threshold in GeV, signal efficiency in percent, predicted trigger rate, latency in us, and margin to the allocated rate."}]}
